recipes.title: Hojicha burnt Basque cheesecake
recipes.description: Roasted tea, a dark caramelised top and a soft centre. A low-air mixing method for a smooth, dense cheesecake.
recipes.tin: 24 × 12 cm rectangular tin, depth not supplied

steps.title: Infuse the hojicha cream
steps.tip: Warm the cream, do not boil.
steps.text: Warm {cream} of pure heavy cream in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Remove from the heat and whisk in {hojicha} of hojicha powder until smooth. Set aside to cool slightly.

steps.title: Prepare the oven and tin
steps.tip: 220°C fan-forced. Use the original tin size for a 1× batch.
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C fan-forced. Crumple a large sheet of baking paper, unfold it and press it into your 24 × 12 cm rectangular tin. Let the paper extend at least 3 cm above the rim to allow for the rise.

steps.title: Mix the base and starch
steps.tip: Keep the mixer on low to avoid adding air.
steps.text: Using a paddle attachment, or a hand mixer on low, mix {cheese} of room-temperature cream cheese, {sugar} of caster sugar and {starch} of potato starch just until smooth and lump-free. Scrape down the bowl halfway through.

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.tip: Add one at a time, mixing only until incorporated.
steps.text: With the mixer on low, add {eggs} and {yolk}, one at a time. Let each addition blend into the base before adding the next. Stop mixing once the last addition disappears.

steps.title: Fold in the cream and salt
steps.tip: Switch to a spatula. Keep it submerged as you stir.
steps.text: Add {salt} of fine sea salt. Pour in the cooled hojicha cream in a slow stream. Stir by hand in wide, slow circles until the batter is uniform, taking care not to whip in air.

steps.title: Strain, rest and pop
steps.text: Pour the batter through a fine-mesh sieve into the prepared tin. Tap the tin on the bench 3 to 4 times. Rest for 3 minutes, then use a toothpick to pop bubbles on the surface.

steps.title: Bake until dark with a wobbly centre
steps.tip: Original guidance: 30 to 35 minutes at 220°C fan-forced.
steps.text: Bake for 30 to 35 minutes. The top should be deep dark brown and caramelised, while the middle 3 inches (about 7.6 cm) still jiggles like set jelly when you nudge the tin. Timing depends on the oven and batter depth.

steps.title: Cool, chill and slice
steps.tip: Chill in the tin for at least 8 hours, or overnight.
steps.text: Cool completely in the tin on a wire rack, then chill in the tin for at least 8 hours or overnight. Use the paper overhang to lift out the firm cake. Slice with a hot, clean chef’s knife, wiping the blade dry between cuts.
